Stephanie — quick update from runtime side.

What I see: around 17:58 PT we had a staged rollout of model-variant v2.1.4 with different quantization kernels enabled for reduced token-cost. Correlation: increased batching queue depth and KV-cache miss ratio on the streaming path for sessions with long-lived context (Orchard uses persistent session windows). p95 jumped ~300ms, p99 jumped 1.2s in the US-west pool.

Prelim mitigation I recommend now:
- Initiate an immediate rollback of the v2.1.4 rollout to v2.1.3 for the affected routing policy (canary/custome-weights).
- Apply a temporary global limit on max_batch_time for streaming hosts (+20ms) and enable aggressive prefix KV caching for sessions older than 30m.
- If rollback is slow, route Orchard's traffic to their Dedicated placeholder pool (we have warm capacity in us-west-2) for the next 4 hours while we validate.

I've attached a Datadog snapshot of queue depth. I can start the rollback now if engineering/ops give green light.

Quick incident summary and request for exec decision: 

What happened: During Orchard Health's evening peak (18:00 PT), their streaming chat p99 latency increased sharply following a staged rollout of model-variant v2.1.4 that used new quantization kernels. This caused SSE reconnections and client timeouts for long-lived sessions.

What we did (chronology):
- 17:12: internal escalation after customer report.
- 17:42: engineering identified correlation with v2.1.4 rollout and queue depth increases.
- 17:50-18:10: rolled back the variant for Orchard routing and applied temporary batch-time and cache settings.
- 18:05: CS offered dedicated routing (customer accepted), cutover completed at ~18:20 PT. Observed p99 restored to baseline within ~10-15 minutes.

Customer impact: elevated p99 and user reconnections for ~30-40 minutes; no data loss reported. Customer is sensitive (triage flows).

Requested exec decisions:
1) Approve expedited allocation of a 3-node reserved Dedicated buffer for Orchard for the next 30 days (to avoid recurrence during scheduled peak windows). Estimated incremental monthly cost: $9,000 — recommend crediting 3 days as goodwill.
2) Approve formal RCA and an engineering change: require an additional canary stage for streaming endpoints (long-lived sessions flag) before quantization kernel rollouts.

I've attached the Datadog and customer logs to the ticket (HS-12764). For the credit I will use my discretionary approvals up to 3 days; beyond that I need finance sign-off.
